nodes.label: Sprint 130.2 - Real Photo Source Download Reliability & Latency Budget
nodes.rationale: Wikimedia rate-limits and never-retry-on-429 policy adopted after live testing showed repeated 429s from upload.wikimedia.org when scenes fired back-to-back; a corrected, reachable-contact User-Agent was identified as a likely contributor to harsher rate limiting.

nodes.label: Sprint 130.1 - Real Photo Source Quality & Reliability Follow-up
Sprint 130 - Wikimedia Commons Real Photo Source for Visuals
Sprint 131+ - Additional Real Photo Sources (Planned)
nodes.rationale: Each additional source (Openverse, Library of Congress/Archive.org, NASA Image and Video Library, Pexels/Pixabay/Unsplash) is scoped as an independent sprint on top of the ADR-019 source-router so none require changing ImageProviderName or VisualAssetPipeline's validation branches again; real stock video sourcing is called out as a separate architectural decision since Visuals only ever produces stills today.

nodes.label: ADR-019: Single 'real' Image Provider with Source Router
nodes.rationale: A single "real" ImageProviderName with an internal, extensible source router (Wikimedia Commons first) was chosen instead of one provider name per source, so future real photo sources extend the router without touching ImageProviderName or VisualAssetPipeline's validation branches.

nodes.label: RealPhotoImageProvider
WikimediaCommonsClient
nodes.rationale: No API key, license allowlist, MIME allowlist, and resolution ranking follow the same fetch/timeout/byte-cap conventions as every other real provider, keeping a single provider-hardening pattern across the codebase.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.43 - Fatih Documentary Live Audio & Assembly Production Run
Sprint 129.41 - Canonical Completed-Stage Regeneration
nodes.rationale: Public regeneration authority was deliberately restricted to fromStage=video only, with arbitrary-stage regeneration left as explicit future work, to keep the initial completed-stage regeneration surface small and provably safe.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.40 - Production Scene-Video Full-Frame Framing Remediation
nodes.rationale: Cover/crop rendering was replaced with a centered, aspect-preserving contained foreground (with cover/crop/zoompan motion kept only in a separate blurred decorative background) so the full source composition stays visible instead of being cropped out.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.39 - Canonical Stage-Bounded Production Resume
Sprint 129.38 - Retry-Budget Settled-Receipt Cross-Stage Replay Remediation
nodes.rationale: Project-wide consumed-receipt selection from failed terminal settlement was removed and bound instead to the current attempt's exact reservation/record/lease/claim/attempt authority, closing a cross-stage replay hole where a receipt for one stage could be mistakenly reused for another.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.37 - Assembly AI Token Budget and Truncation Remediation
nodes.rationale: A bounded, per-stage OPENAI_ASSEMBLY_MAX_TOKENS (default 3200, inclusive 1600-6000) was added, mirroring the earlier per-stage token-budget pattern, so assembly's AI planning call fails closed on truncation instead of silently producing malformed output.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.36 - Explicit One-Time Retry Budget Extension Authority
nodes.rationale: Ordinal-5 retry attempts are unconditionally rejected and a retry-budget extension requires a single-use, cryptographically bound authority record (not a config flag), so extending the budget for one failed attempt can never be silently reused for a later unrelated failure.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.35 - Legacy Terminal Lineage Global-Quiescence Compatibility Remediation
Sprint 129.33 - Exhausted Retry Admission / Final TOCTOU Remediation
nodes.rationale: Canonical shared-path check-then-delete cleanup was removed in favor of an operation-owned quarantine primitive, closing a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race in lock/gate/stale cleanup.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.32 - Exact job.attempts Invariant for Failed Retry Durable Attempt Selection
Sprint 129.30 - Failed-Terminal Evidence and Retry Boundary Hardening
Sprint 129.29 - Failed-Terminal Settlement Remediation
nodes.rationale: A canonical failed-settlement callback completes lease release, claim abandon, record cancellation, and recovery/quiescence validation in one sequence so a failed attempt's durable authorities never linger half-released.

nodes.label: Runtime Backup Long-Path, V3 Runtime Authority & Trusted Backup Root
nodes.rationale: V3 backup manifests use a canonical source runtime authority and unchanging runtime-tree-sha256-v1 aggregate contract; V1/V2 legacy formats are retained read-only for portability but same-authority restore from them fails closed, so authority binding can never be silently downgraded.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.28 - Production Acceptance Reauthorization and Durable Identity Authority Hardening
nodes.rationale: Canonical identity is built only from completed durable readback (never from pre-plan/request/fallback authority) and completed-preparation tokens are frozen and WeakMap-owned, so a forged or cloned token can never acquire capability.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.27 - Audio Atomicity, Compensation & Publication Hardening
nodes.rationale: Two-phase publication with a PortableNoClobberFilePublisher and typed AudioCanonicalAdmissionConflictError separates security rejection from normal failure, so a foreign-file conflict is preserved rather than treated as an ordinary retryable error.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.25 C.2B.4 - Operation-Scoped Runtime Context Propagation
Sprint 129.25 C.2B.3 - Production Storage Relocation Audit
nodes.rationale: A mutation-free audit catalogued 28 production storage entrypoint families (11 READY, 7 REQUIRES ADAPTER, 1 REQUIRES MIGRATION, 5 REQUIRES POLICY DECISION, 4 BLOCKING) before any relocation/cutover work, so runtime root relocation cannot begin without first proving every entrypoint's blast radius.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.25 C.2B.2 - Verified Migration Candidate Creation
nodes.rationale: Candidate bytes are sourced only from a verified backup payload, never a live runtime copy, so a migration candidate can never silently diverge from the last verified backup.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.25 C.2B.1 - Migration Candidate Schema, Preflight & Verifier
Sprint 129.25 C.2A - Guarded Filesystem Foundation
nodes.rationale: Centralized RuntimeProtectedRoots/RuntimePathPolicy/GuardedRuntimeFilesystem primitives give every later runtime-mutating sprint (backup, migration, relocation) a single reparse-aware, containment-checked write path instead of each reimplementing safe writes.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.25 C.1 - Verified Runtime Backup Foundation
Sprint 129.25B.1 - Targeted Runtime Storage Hardening
Sprint 129.25B - Runtime Root Abstraction & Tracking Policy Foundation
nodes.rationale: ATOLYE_RUNTIME_ROOT was introduced as a configurable storage root (defaulting to the legacy process.cwd()/data/projects) specifically so a later zero-tracked-runtime policy (Sprint 129.25C) could be introduced without an immediate breaking migration.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.24 - Existing Acceptance Marker Portability
Sprint 129.22 - Animation Structured Output Diagnosis and Hardening
nodes.rationale: The animation provider contract was narrowed to only motionType/start/end/transition, with platform-owned fields (sceneId, sourceImageAssetId, durationSeconds, createdAt) derived from trusted context after validation instead of echoed by the AI provider, closing a class of strict-schema-vs-echo mismatch failures.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.21 - Animation Failure Propagation & Diagnostic Hardening
nodes.rationale: AnimationAssetPipeline was converting known provider/scene/phase errors into a generic code, losing the real failure reason; AnimationMotionPlanError now carries safe, specific evidence (sceneId, phase, provider/model, HTTP status, finish reason) instead.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.20 - Visuals Truncation Propagation & Stage Token Budget
nodes.rationale: VisualManager was not propagating the observed AI_RESPONSE_TRUNCATED error code before parsing, so a truncated response was misclassified as AI_RESPONSE_INVALID_JSON; a bounded OPENAI_VISUALS_MAX_TOKENS (2000-6000) was added alongside the fix.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.19 - Visuals Structured Output and Application-Owned Timestamp Hardening
nodes.rationale: createdAt was moved from provider-supplied to application-owned across research/script/visuals so a provider emitting an unexpected timestamp field could no longer fail strict schema validation after an otherwise-complete, non-truncated response.

nodes.label: Sprint 41 - Animation Scene-Level Regeneration
Sprint 42 - Video Engine Foundation
Sprint 43 - Audio Engine Foundation
Sprint 44 - Assembly Engine Foundation
Sprint 48 - Final Pipeline Integration
Sprint 49 - Real AI Provider Integration Guardrails
Sprint 54 - Pipeline Retry & Resume Planning Foundation
Sprint 64 - Pipeline Queue / Job Management Foundation
Sprint 66 - Pipeline Queue Scheduler
Sprint 77 - Pipeline Execution History Foundation
Sprint 83 - Pipeline Job State Consistency
nodes.rationale: A centralized, rule-based job transition model (queued->running/cancelled, running->completed/failed/cancelled, failed/cancelled->queued retry, completed terminal) replaced ad hoc status writes, closing races between cancellation and in-flight persistence.

nodes.label: Sprint 93 - Pipeline Orchestration Foundation
nodes.rationale: getNextPipelineStage() only fires downstream job creation after a running->completed transition, and completed source plus the missing downstream queued job are persisted in the same atomic write, keeping the deterministic one-job-per-project-per-stage model idempotent under retries and concurrent completion.

nodes.label: Sprint 98.0 - Production Execution Persistence Adapter Foundation
nodes.rationale: A frozen schema v1 persistence adapter (transaction, operation journal, idempotency, reservation) was built and left disabled/preview-only, deliberately deferring dispatch/execution/provider/worker/UI wiring to later sprints.

nodes.label: Sprint 99.1 - Durable Storage Recovery & Index Hardening
nodes.rationale: The content-addressed lookup index is explicitly a derived artifact rebuilt deterministically from canonical records, never an authorization or business-decision source, so a missing or corrupt index can never itself grant or deny execution.

nodes.label: Sprint 100 - Durable Lease & Worker Ownership Foundation
Sprint 101 - Durable Execution Claim & Recovery Coordination
Sprint 102 - Durable Execution Attempt & Outcome Journal Foundation
Sprint 103 - Production Execution Coordinator Foundation
Sprint 104 - Durable Attempt Lifecycle Foundation
Sprint 105 - Durable Worker Execution Foundation
nodes.rationale: The handler is called exactly once and only a safe serializable summary is persisted to the journal, so raw error stacks, secrets, or uncontrolled payloads can never leak into durable records.

nodes.label: Sprint 106 - Pipeline Stage Durable Execution Integration
nodes.rationale: PipelineRunner.runStage was wrapped with an optional durable adapter so legacy behavior is preserved when the adapter is absent, letting the durable layer be integrated without a second orchestrator.

nodes.label: Sprint 107 - Durable Pipeline Composition Root Wiring
nodes.rationale: ATOLYE_DURABLE_PIPELINE_EXECUTION=enabled gates the durable adapter so legacy behavior is preserved by default while all pipeline run/retry/resume entrypoints share one composition factory.

nodes.label: Sprint 108 - Durable Recovery Bootstrap Integration
nodes.rationale: This sprint closed the Sprint 99-108 Durable Production Execution phase; bootstrapRecovery classifies durable attempts write-free and never itself reschedules terminal attempts.

nodes.label: Sprint 109 - Process Startup Bootstrap Integration
Sprint 110 - Production Worker Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: A created->starting->ready->draining->stopped/failed state model ensures a worker cannot become ready until recovery initialization and verification are fully successful, avoiding a partially-initialized worker accepting work.

nodes.label: Sprint 112 - Production Runtime Health API
Sprint 113 - Production Visual Asset Pipeline Activation
Sprint 114 - Production Narration Audio Pipeline Activation
Sprint 115 - Production Video Assembly Activation
Sprint 116 - Animation Motion Plan Production Contract
nodes.rationale: Animation stage was redefined to produce a scene-level motion-plan artifact (schemaVersion 2, artifactType motion-plan, no filePath/url) rather than physical media, keeping physical rendering concentrated in the Video stage instead of duplicating a media-rendering path.

nodes.label: Sprint 117 - Production Scene Video Rendering Activation
Sprint 118 - Assembly Scene-Video Consumption
nodes.rationale: Stream-copy is only attempted when scene/narration duration differs by at most 1/30s and codec/profile/timebase match exactly; otherwise the scene is clone-pad/trim re-encoded, keeping fast-path assembly from silently producing drifted output.

nodes.label: Sprint 119 - Pipeline Retry Continuation Hardening
nodes.rationale: continueProject() is bounded and non-recursive, running at most one stage per call, specifically to close a race where concurrent dispatchers could jump past the assembly boundary into thumbnail.

nodes.label: Sprint 120 - Production Thumbnail Pipeline Activation
Sprint 121 - Production YouTube Package Pipeline Activation
Sprint 122 - Production YouTube Publish Pipeline Foundation
nodes.rationale: Provider explicit failure never produces false-success, and on an indeterminate timeout/upload the publishing intent is preserved rather than automatically retried, to avoid a duplicate remote video upload.

nodes.label: Sprint 123 - Production End-to-End Stabilization
nodes.rationale: An atomic youtube-publish-recovery.json receipt is written before the canonical publish result, so a crash after a successful remote upload but before canonical persistence can be promoted to canonical on restart without a second upload.

nodes.label: Sprint 124 - Production Publish Reconciliation Hardening
nodes.rationale: reconcilePublish only ever promotes a `matched` result to canonical published state and never itself starts an upload, using priority order canonical published -> recovery receipt -> publishing intent reconciliation.

nodes.label: Sprint 125 - Production End-to-End Validation
nodes.rationale: The full canonical stage order (Research through Export) was run end-to-end via the real PipelineRunner.run() entrypoint on a deterministic fixture rather than a second validation harness, so the same production wiring is exercised rather than a parallel one.

nodes.label: Sprint 126 - Real Production Acceptance Run Preparation
nodes.rationale: ProductionReadinessService defines READY/NOT_CONFIGURED/INVALID/UNAVAILABLE/BLOCKED so overall ready=true can only be produced when every critical check is READY; readiness itself never makes a paid provider call or mutates user projects.

nodes.label: Sprint 127 - Production Animation Provider Activation
nodes.rationale: OpenAIAnimationProvider validates the motion-plan JSON against an exact-key schema with prototype-pollution and depth limits and never determines scene/source identity or file locators itself, keeping identity/locator authority in AnimationStorage.

nodes.label: Sprint 128.1 - Production Acceptance P0 Closure and Operator Entrypoint
Sprint 128.2 - Production Acceptance P1 Hardening
Sprint 129 - Production Environment Binding and Readiness-Only Machine Validation
Sprint 129.5 - Production Acceptance Topic Input Contract
nodes.rationale: The execute CLI now requires an explicit --topic and removed the built-in production topic fallback, and slug is deterministic from topic+runId, so a resume can never silently pick up a different topic than the original run.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.7 - Research Structured Output Reliability Hardening
nodes.rationale: The first paid production execute produced a successful, non-fallback OpenAI call that still failed strict artifact validation; createdAt was removed from the research provider schema and application-owned canonically instead, and OPENAI_RESEARCH_MAX_TOKENS (default 3200, 1600-6000) was added.

nodes.label: Sprint 129.9 - Failed-Stage Resume Reconciliation Hardening
nodes.rationale: Resume no longer sends a failed start stage directly to the scheduler; a shared prepareFailedStageRetry primitive performs durable reconciliation and CAS-controlled job preparation first, closing a path where a failed job required manual retry and the CLI closed with PRODUCTION_ACCEPTANCE_EXECUTION_FAILED without starting any stage.

nodes.label: Production Acceptance Execution Gate
nodes.rationale: Recurring pattern across the 129.x remediation sprints: passing regression suites and independent review does not itself authorize spending real provider credits or mutating the real production project - a separate, explicit operator authorization step is always required before real production execution, consistent with the codebase's fail-closed design.
